question: Can changing the signal improve returns and stability, rather than just reducing leverage?

rules.direction_confirmed_volume: volume leg longs require positive 14-day return, shorts require negative 14-day return; rank volume descending on both sides; each leg 0.5 if enough eligible names; blend equally with momentum, renormalize

promotion: Price coverage required; both 2023-24 and 2025-26 Sharpe must improve, costs stressed, maxT FWER<.05 over all candidates, previous search history and missing funding still prohibit strong discovery claims; recent week not selection criterion
known_limitations: daily open proxy for real 00:05 execution
historical splits already observed, not pristine OOS

second_batch_before_execution.trigger: STRK long supported by stale 14d strength despite daily selloff; volume-only weak in 2026
second_batch_before_execution.rules: Veto wrong-sign long/short weights after forming baseline, shrink larger leg to keep dollar-neutral without refilling freed risk. No renormalization after veto. Third candidate uses raw average of factor books without post-cancellation normalization.
second_batch_before_execution.multiplicity: Include all first and second batch candidates in common maxT family; adaptive extension is exploratory, not pristine preregistration.

third_batch_before_execution.question: Do weak factors need an explicit rule to stop receiving money?
third_batch_before_execution.rule: Use only previous 90 fully completed daily net paper returns of separate momentum-only and volume-only books; no lookback search. During first 90 days of each reset window use baseline. Volume health removes volume if its trailing net mean <=0; momentum remains. Both-factor health allocates only to positive-mean books, and stays flat if neither passes. Rescale selected book to original gross. Paper net returns exclude historical funding, which remains a deployment block.
third_batch_before_execution.multiplicity: Recompute common maxT over all 12 variants; exploratory adaptive batch, not confirmatory.
